paper_metadata.title: Effect of TiN on the microstructure and mechanical property of As-cast TiZrNbVAl lightweight high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: The grain size of as-cast light weight high entropy alloy (LHEA) is required to be refined and its mechanical property should be improved further to satisfy its engineering application.

Non-equiatomic TiZrNbVAl LHEA with different TiN addition (0, 3, and 5 wt%) were prepared by the levitation melting furnace in argon atmosphere. Hereafter, they were named as TiN-0, TiN-3 and TiN-5 alloy, respectively.

Non-equiatomic TiZrNbVAl LHEA with different TiN addition (0, 3, and 5 wt%) were prepared by the levitation melting furnace in argon atmosphere.
In order to ensure the elemental uniformity of the ingot, each ingot was melted three times, and the alloy ingot was flipped before each melting.
Then, TiN was uniformly put to the surrounding of the ingot and the ingot was melt again and hold for 30 s followed by furnace cooling.

The yield strength of TiN-0 is 803 MPa and the compression strength is 2274 MPa.
The yield strength of TiN-0 is 803 MPa and the compression strength is 2274 MPa.
When the TiN content is increased to 3 wt%, the yield strength is increased to 1603 MPa, an increase of 2 times.
However, compared with TiN-0, the compression ductility decreased from more than 50 % to 24.6 ± 3.2 %, which was reduced by more than half.
Furthermore, the yield strength of TiN-5 is 2124 MPa, which is almost 3 times larger than that of the original alloy.
However, due to the segregation of TiN at grain boundaries, the compression ductility of TiN-5 LHEA is limited, only 2.7 ± 0.4 %.
